Antifungals 517 Choice of Antifungal, p.517 Aspergillosis, p.517 Blastomycosis, p.518 Candidiasis, p.518 Chromoblastomycosis, p.518 Coccidioidomycosis, p.518 Cryptococcosis, p.519 Dermatophytoses, p.519 Endocarditis, p.519 Eye infections, p.519 Histoplasmosis, p.519 Infections in immunocompromised patients, p.520 Meningitis, p.520 Mucormycosis, p.520 Mycetoma, p.520 Nail infections, p.520 Paracoccidioidomycosis, p.520 Peritonitis, p.521 Pityriasis versicolor, p.521 Pneumocystis pneumonia, p.521 Protothecosis, p.521 Respiratory-tract infections, p.521 Skin infections, p.521 Sporotrichosis, p.522 Tinea, p.522 This chapter describes the drugs that are used mainly in the treatment and prophylaxis of fungal infections (mycoses). They include: • the azole derivatives, including: • imidazoles (such as ketoconazole) • triazoles (such as fluconazole, itraconazole, posa- conazole, and voriconazole) • the allylamines (naftifine and terbinafine) • the echinocandins (such as caspofungin and mi- cafungin) • several polyene antibiotics (including amphotericin B and nystatin) • other antifungal antibiotics (for example griseoful- vin) • other compounds such as amorolfine, ciclopirox olamine, flucytosine, haloprogin, tolnaftate, and un- decenoic acid and its salts. Choice of Antifungal Fungi may be classified as yeasts or moulds according to their appearance and means of growth. Examples of yeasts are Candida and Cryptococcus spp., while moulds include Aspergillus spp., the dermatophytes, and the Mucorales fungi. Some fungi are termed di- morphic as they appear to be yeast-like in the host, but grow as moulds in vitro. Blastomycosis, chromoblast- omycosis, coccidioidomycosis, histoplasmosis, para- coccidioidomycosis, and sporotrichosis are examples of diseases caused by dimorphic fungi.
